question: About what percentage of passenger traffic is carried by roads in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.87**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• In India, roads are the most preferred mode of transportation for passengers, carrying a significant portion of passenger traffic.

• Approximately 87% of passenger traffic in India is carried by roads, highlighting the dominance of road transport in the country.

• Roads provide door-to-door service, which is a major advantage over other modes of transport.

• The extensive network of roads in India, including national highways, state highways, and rural roads, facilitates connectivity and accessibility across various regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Passenger Traffic**

• Passenger traffic refers to the movement of people from one place to another, typically measured in terms of the number of passengers or passenger-kilometers.

• It is a crucial indicator of the demand for transportation services in a country.

• **Modes of Transport**

• There are various modes of transport, including road, rail, air, and water transport.

• Each mode has its advantages and disadvantages in terms of cost, speed, accessibility, and convenience.

• **Road Transport**

• Road transport involves the movement of passengers and goods using vehicles such as cars, buses, trucks, and motorcycles.

• It is the most flexible mode of transport, providing last-mile connectivity and door-to-door service.

• India has an extensive network of roads, including national highways, state highways, district roads, and rural roads.

• Road transport plays a vital role in the economic development of a country by facilitating trade, commerce, and tourism.

• **National Highways**

• National highways are the primary roadways in India, connecting major cities, ports, and industrial hubs.

• They are managed and maintained by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).
